distillation_scope.leaf_granularity: specific clinical leaf for infection in the spinal epidural space, including hematogenous, contiguous, and procedure-associated presentations
distillation_scope.ranking_note: Presentation ranking should use fever, back or neck pain, neurologic findings, systemic inflammation, bacteremia/source context, and presentation-time MRI/CT evidence when available. Final organism identity and operative culture are confirmatory unless already observed as presentation microbiology context.

latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Bacteria reach the spinal epidural space by bacteremia, adjacent vertebral or paraspinal infection, urinary or skin source, injection drug use, spinal procedure, catheter or device infection, or less commonly direct extension.
Microbial growth and neutrophilic inflammation in epidural fat and venous plexus create phlegmon or abscess, with longitudinal spread across spinal levels.

Epidural pressure, paraspinal inflammation, vertebral or disc involvement, periosteal irritation, and nerve-root inflammation cause severe focal back or neck pain, spinal tenderness, radicular pain, and high CRP or ESR.

Deep bacterial infection and bacteremia trigger fever or chills, tachycardia, leukocytosis or blunted WBC response, elevated CRP/ESR, lactate elevation, hyponatremia in severe illness, and sepsis physiology.

Staphylococcus aureus, gram-negative urinary-source bacteremia, procedure-related inoculation, and other invasive pathogens may seed or maintain epidural infection; blood cultures may be positive before abscess culture confirms the organism.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Cord, root, or cauda equina compression and ischemia
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Epidural collection, canal stenosis, vascular congestion, thrombophlebitis, or local inflammatory myelopathy injures roots, cauda equina, or spinal cord, causing weakness, sensory loss, gait impairment, sphincter dysfunction, or respiratory failure in high cervical disease.

Large epidural abscess, paraspinal or psoas extension, vertebral osteomyelitis, resistant organism, delayed diagnosis, or uncontrolled urinary/skin/endovascular source sustains infection despite antibiotics.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Septic organ dysfunction from epidural infection
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: High bacterial burden, bacteremia, or delayed source control can produce encephalopathy, AKI, shock, hypoxemia, and elevated mortality hazard.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: An epidural collection narrows the canal depending on size and location.
Canal compromise is the direct imaging substrate for cord, root, or cauda equina compression.
Compression and vascular compromise drive weakness, sensory loss, gait impairment, or sphincter dysfunction.
New or progressive neurologic deficit creates emergency decompression risk.
Delayed decompression in compressive SEA increases risk of permanent neurologic injury.
Paraspinal collections signal a drainable or surgically relevant nidus.
High source-control need without adequate drainage sustains infection.
Adequate decompression or drainage lowers uncontrolled abscess hazard.
Fever history and measured temperature partially covary but may diverge in afebrile or pretreated SEA.
Both reflect pyogenic spinal inflammation, with ESR often lagging.
Sepsis physiology links hyperlactatemia with hypotension or hypoperfusion.
Positive blood cultures may indicate ongoing bacteremic seeding or an uncontrolled nidus.
Severe neurologic injury, immobility, respiratory failure, and complications increase mortality hazard.
Shock is a major mortality driver in severe SEA.

treatments.treatment_name: Empiric intravenous anti-staphylococcal plus gram-negative coverage
treatments.context_specific_role: Initial antimicrobial vector field while blood culture, MRI, neurologic status, and source-control needs are being clarified.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Inactive empiric therapy cannot reliably reduce bacterial burden.
Large abscess or compression may not clear with antibiotics alone.

treatments.context_specific_role: Definitive organism- and susceptibility-directed therapy after microbiologic context is known; duration depends on abscess drainage, osteomyelitis, bacteremia persistence, and host risk.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Persistent bacteremia raises concern for endovascular or undrained source.

treatments.treatment_name: Urgent surgical decompression and epidural abscess drainage
treatments.context_specific_role: Reduces compressive mass effect and source-control failure when neurologic deficit, severe canal compromise, large abscess, deformity, instability, or failure of medical therapy is present.
Diagnostic and source-control option when a drainable paraspinal, psoas, or accessible epidural-related collection exists and neurologic compromise does not mandate open decompression.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Compressive neurologic deficit generally requires decompression rather than aspiration alone.

treatments.treatment_name: Remote source control for urinary, skin, catheter, or endovascular focus
treatments.context_specific_role: Treats the upstream source that seeded or sustains epidural infection when a urinary tract, skin/soft tissue, catheter, endocarditis, or other focus is present.

treatments.treatment_name: Sepsis supportive care with hemodynamic, oxygen, and renal support
treatments.context_specific_role: Stabilizes physiology while antibiotics and source control reduce the infectious vector field.
Does not eradicate infection, but changes detection latency for neurologic deterioration and supports recovery after decompression or medical control.

present.trajectory_modulation: Raises invasive bacterial infection risk and worsens septic and neurologic reserve.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Diabetes increases susceptibility to invasive infection.
Diabetes increases complication and mortality risk.

risk_factors.clinical_rationale: Diabetes increases invasive bacterial infection risk and worsens neurologic and septic outcomes.

present.trajectory_modulation: Raises bacteremia and skin-source seeding probability.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Skin and bloodstream inoculation pathways are common in SEA.
Skin-source bacteremia may seed epidural infection.

risk_factors.clinical_rationale: Skin and bloodstream inoculation pathways are common in SEA.

present.trajectory_modulation: Direct inoculation increases epidural seeding probability.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Procedure-associated inoculation is a direct route into epidural or adjacent spinal spaces.

risk_factors.clinical_rationale: Direct inoculation or procedure-associated bacteremia can seed the epidural space.

present.trajectory_modulation: Raises vulnerability and may blunt fever or WBC response while increasing complications.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Immunosuppressed patients may be afebrile despite deep infection.
Host response can be blunted or altered by immunosuppression.
Poor reserve raises mortality and complication hazard.

risk_factors.clinical_rationale: Host vulnerability raises risk and may blunt fever/WBC while increasing complications.

present.trajectory_modulation: Raises emergency decompression and irreversible neurologic injury hazards.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Cord-level compression has less neurologic reserve.
Progressive cord-level deficit creates urgent decompression risk.
Cord compression can cause permanent injury if not decompressed promptly.

risk_factors.clinical_rationale: Cord-level compression is more time-critical than isolated pain without deficit.

present.trajectory_modulation: Allows longitudinal abscess spread, persistent bacteremia, and source-control failure.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Delay allows abscess expansion and persistent nidus.
Inadequate early therapy can sustain bacteremia.

risk_factors.clinical_rationale: Diagnostic delay permits longitudinal abscess spread and neurologic deterioration.

supportive_care: early MRI with contrast when feasible; CT may expose collection but MRI better defines compression
blood cultures before antibiotics when this does not delay unstable care
quality_notes: No first-line/preferred labels are included; treatment ranking should emerge from RMST simulation and context axes.
Final organism identity, operative culture, and biopsy are not required ranking evidence; they are workup/context evidence when observed.

SEA-specific anatomic axes are disease-owned here because the atlas already has separate VO and Brucella epidural-abscess axes. Shared physiologic, neurologic, microbiology, and source-control axes are reused where existing names are stable.
